qualification.scope: strict TS types, solid boolean generated vertices, open surface, Zod schema rejection, repeated-byte GLB and buffer roundtrip only

embedded_payload_reviews.name: sharp/libvips image-processing closure
embedded_payload_reviews.reason: manifold-3d → @gltf-transform/functions → ndarray-pixels → sharp; package metadata alone conceals native bundled component obligations
embedded_payload_reviews.license_findings: Installed package README lists LGPLv3 components including libvips/GLib/font libraries, MPL-2.0 cairo, BSD/FTL/fontconfig/libpng/TIFF/IJG/zlib/MIT components and AOM patent terms. Aggregate npm LGPL metadata is not a complete bundle SPDX/SBOM. No image processing is imported by the qualification fixture.
embedded_payload_reviews.decision: local unused transitive package only; no redistributable SDK/runtime bundle approval; collect all licenses/notices and exact corresponding sources before any redistribution

embedded_payload_reviews.name: Manifold WASM / esbuild / meshoptimizer / Rapier
embedded_payload_reviews.license_findings: Compiled payloads remain executable build input. Direct package licenses and hashes inspected; complete native/WASM binary source-to-payload provenance and bundled notices are a separate distribution gate. Rapier and meshoptimizer presence comes from upstream dependencies and grants no game physics/optimizer capability.
embedded_payload_reviews.decision: Manifold WASM and esbuild executable qualified only for local trusted fixture; no untrusted-sandbox or compiled-payload redistribution approval.

license_review_limits: No automatic vulnerability-free or supply-chain-safe claim follows from matching registry integrity. Registry signatures/attestations are preserved in private metadata, not independently verified in this review.

All 120 exact package registry licenses, integrity values, platform conditions and lifecycle entrypoints were reviewed. License/notice text present in the 50 installed packages was identified; missing notices are explicit. Other platform binaries were not executed or individually extracted.

The installed esbuild platform helper inherits MIT evidence from its exact registry record and the parent esbuild LICENSE. @jscadui/3mf-export and @nodable/entities publish MIT metadata but lack a top-level license file in the inspected tarball; collect upstream notices before distribution.
The libvips README is the bundle-license evidence where no top-level LICENSE is included. Future packaging must not assume LGPL-3.0-or-later is the only applicable license.
A packaged developer SDK would redistribute tools and must separately satisfy their terms. Keeping tools out of the base runtime does not waive that requirement.
